lesson.text: Quick memory: which notes make the F major chord? (F, A and C.) Today: playing a melody with one hand and its chords with the other.
Fingers have numbers: the thumb is 1 and the little finger is 5, on both hands. Music often prints small finger numbers over the notes.
C position: put your right thumb on middle C and one finger on each white key: C, D, E, F, G for fingers 1 to 5. Your left little finger (5) goes on the C below, and your left thumb (1) on G.
The right hand usually plays the melody and the left hand the chords. With the left hand, the C major chord is C, E and G, played with fingers 5, 3 and 1.
Choose the chord that fits: the melody's notes should belong to it. In C major, E fits the C chord (C, E, G) and A fits F (F, A, C). B or D fit G (G, B, D).
Worked example: the melody E, D, C over the C chord. E and C are in the C chord; D is a passing note, a quick step between them.
Keep a steady beat, look ahead to the next chord, and practise hands separately, then together, slowly at first.
Try it in the world: on any keyboard, play Frère Jacques (C, D, E, C) with the right hand while the left holds the C chord. Next: instruments of the world.

exercises.prompt: Your right thumb is on C. Which finger plays the marked key?
exercises.hint: Count up from the thumb, one finger a key.
exercises.explain: Thumb on C (1), D is 2, E is 3.

exercises.prompt: On both hands, the thumb is finger 1.
exercises.explain: True: the thumbs are 1 and the little fingers 5.
1 is the thumb, so 5 is the little finger.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Is this one note or a chord?
exercises.hint: Can you hear more than one pitch at once?
exercises.explain: Three notes sounded together, C, E and G: a chord.

exercises.prompt: Listen. Is this chord major or minor?
exercises.hint: Bright or darker? Listen to the middle note.
exercises.explain: It is C, E and G: 4 semitones from C to E, so it is major.

exercises.prompt: Which chord fits under the melody note A, in C major?
exercises.hint: Which chord has A in it? C is C, E, G; F is F, A, C; G is G, B, D.
exercises.explain: A is in the F chord (F, A, C).

exercises.prompt: Which chord fits under the melody note B, in C major?
exercises.hint: Which chord has B in it?
exercises.explain: B is in the G chord (G, B, D).

exercises.prompt: Your left little finger is on C, in C position. Which finger plays the marked G?
exercises.hint: Your little finger is 5 on C. Count down one finger for each white key up.
exercises.explain: C is 5, D 4, E 3, F 2 and G 1: the thumb.

exercises.prompt: Listen: a melody note with a chord under it. Which chord is it?
exercises.explain: C, E and G are under the melody's E: the C chord.

exercises.hint: Its lowest note is its name.
exercises.explain: F, A and C: the F chord.

exercises.prompt: The left hand usually plays the melody.
exercises.explain: False: the right hand usually plays the melody, the left the chords.

exercises.prompt: Which chord fits under this bar of melody?
exercises.hint: Every note of the bar should be in the chord.
exercises.explain: G, B and D are all in the G chord (G, B, D), so it fits every note. The C chord shares only G, and the F chord shares none of them.

exercises.prompt: Which chord fits under this bar of melody?
exercises.hint: Every note of the bar should be in the chord.
exercises.explain: F, A and C are all in the F chord (F, A, C). The C chord shares only C, and the G chord shares none of them.

exercises.prompt: Listen: three chords. In which order did they come?
exercises.hint: Name each chord by its lowest note.
exercises.explain: F (F, A, C), then C (C, E, G), then G (G, B, D).

exercises.prompt: In C position, the right hand covers C to G. How many white keys is that?
exercises.explain: C, D, E, F, G: 5 keys, one for each finger.

exercises.prompt: Put these in the best order for learning a new piece.
exercises.hint: Start easy, then add, then speed up.
exercises.explain: Hands separately first, then together slowly, then at full speed.

exercises.prompt: Which chord do these left-hand fingers play?
exercises.hint: Read the keys under the numbers.
exercises.explain: Fingers 5, 3 and 1 on C, E and G: the C major chord.

exercises.prompt: Listen: the melody ends on C over the C chord. In right-hand C position, which finger plays that last C?
exercises.hint: Where is your right thumb in C position?
exercises.explain: The thumb (1) sits on middle C.

exercises.prompt: Match each bar of melody to the chord that fits under it.
exercises.hint: The C chord is C, E, G; the F chord F, A, C; the G chord G, B, D.
exercises.explain: E, G and C are all in the C chord. A, F and C are all in the F chord. B, D and G are all in the G chord. When every melody note is in the chord, it fits.
